proposals.label: Smit et al. (2008)
proposals.rationale: Smit et al. (2008) report the first familial occurrence in this entry, a heterozygous MPZ mutation confirmed in two generations. The variants already in the entry were all de novo in single patients. This supports autosomal dominant transmission, but the abstract does not specify the variant or give follow-up details.

evidence.statement: Smit et al. (2008) noted that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition with prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia. Histopathology shows absent or thin myelin sheaths, and most of the few reported patients die within the first years of life. Mutations had been described in the MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2 genes.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia.
Most of the few patients described in literature die within the first years of life. Histopathologically there are no or thin myelin sheaths.
Mutations have been described in the following genes, MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2.

proposals.label: Kochanski et al. (2004)
proposals.rationale: Kochanski et al. (2004) reported a new MPZ mutation, thr124-to-lys (T124K), that is not in the entry's variant table. They also described sural nerve biopsy findings the entry does not record: nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons, basal lamina onion bulbs and no myelin breakdown products.

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) described the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy, a severe neuropathy with onset in early infancy. Sural nerve biopsy showed the characteristic findings of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and no myelin breakdown products.

proposals.label: Nowakowski and Kochański (2004)
proposals.rationale: Nowakowski and Kochański (2004) report a new MPZ variant, T124K, in a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy. The entry's variant table lists only Q215X and the complex deletion/insertion at nucleotides 550-552. Their E56K finding is in CMT2, a different disorder, so it is not relevant here.

paragraphs.text: Nowakowski and Kochański (2004) screened the coding and promoter sequences of the MPZ gene by SSCP and heteroduplex analysis in patients with CMT1, CMT2, and congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN). They identified a thr124-to-lys (T124K) substitution in MPZ in 1 patient with CHN.
